readingImages.title: The Delaware River at Philadelphia
readingImages.caption: Looking west from Camden toward Philadelphia, April 2025. A present-day view of the river landscape; it does not reconstruct Lenape settlements.

readingImages.title: Independence Hall — historic postcard
readingImages.caption: Historic postcard of Independence Hall; date not recorded. This later depiction is not a view of the Declaration’s adoption in 1776.

readingImages.title: The Constitution — first page
readingImages.caption: First page of the Constitution of the United States, signed in 1787. The document supplies the visual evidence for this reading about governmental structure.

readingImages.title: The President’s House — memorial to the enslaved
readingImages.caption: The Memorial to the Enslaved at the President’s House site, photographed in June 2022. A place of remembrance connected to Ona Judge’s story, not a portrait of her.

readingImages.title: Mother Bethel A.M.E. Church
readingImages.caption: The surviving Mother Bethel church, photographed in 2014. This is a later building in the congregation’s history, not its original converted blacksmith’s shop.

readingImages.title: The Centennial Exhibition opens
readingImages.caption: Published illustration of opening-day ceremonies at Philadelphia’s Centennial Exhibition, May 10, 1876. Historical artwork rather than a photograph.

readingImages.title: Independence Hall’s tower
readingImages.caption: The tower of Independence Hall viewed from the south in 2017. Its appearance provides a starting point for examining alteration and restoration.

readingImages.title: The Liberty Bell and national memory
readingImages.caption: The Liberty Bell displayed across from Independence Hall, October 2016. A present-day symbol for the reading’s question about what an anniversary should remember.

readingImages.title: The Mississippi curves through New Orleans
readingImages.caption: Aerial view of New Orleans and the Mississippi River, April 2007. Geographic context for Bulbancha’s longer history, not an image of the place before colonization.

readingImages.title: The Port of New Orleans
readingImages.caption: A container ship at the Napoleon Avenue terminal, April 2007. A modern view illustrating the port’s continuing function; the Louisiana Purchase occurred in 1803.

readingImages.title: Congo Square — modern view
readingImages.caption: A modern photograph of Congo Square. It shows the place, not a reconstruction of its early gatherings.

readingImages.title: A slave-auction advertisement, 1856
readingImages.caption: A New Orleans auction broadside dated February 23, 1856, naming people offered for sale. Primary-source evidence of slavery and the city’s trade in human beings; its dehumanizing language is historical evidence.
readingImages.credit: J.A. Beard & May, New Orleans, slave auctioneers. Bulletin Print, 35 Gravier St., New Orleans

readingImages.title: Mardi Gras morning in Tremé
readingImages.caption: A Tremé neighborhood street on Mardi Gras morning, February 13, 2018. Contemporary place and cultural context rather than a scene from the beginnings of jazz.

readingImages.title: King Oliver, circa 1915
readingImages.caption: Historical portrait of jazz musician King Oliver, circa 1915. Oliver’s work connects the New Orleans story to the movement of jazz and Louis Armstrong’s career.

readingImages.title: Hurricane Katrina from space
readingImages.caption: NASA satellite image of Hurricane Katrina on August 28, 2005. A view of the storm itself, not a photograph of damage or recovery in New Orleans.

readingImages.title: A living parade tradition
readingImages.caption: Participants in the Big 9 parade on St. Claude Avenue, New Orleans, December 21, 2008. A specific example of the city’s continuing public musical culture.

readingImages.title: The Detroit River meets Lake Erie
readingImages.caption: NOAA aerial image showing the Detroit River’s southern entrance and northeastern Lake Erie. Geographic context for the waterway, not a photograph of early settlement.

readingImages.title: Ford Piquette Avenue Plant
readingImages.caption: The surviving plant’s front exterior. This is the building where the first Model Ts were produced, not a view of assembly-line work.

readingImages.title: Second Baptist Church of Detroit
readingImages.caption: The church exterior, photographed in July 2008. A surviving institution for a reading about the support networks that make arrival possible.

readingImages.title: Rivera Court — industry on the walls
readingImages.caption: A 2025 interior view of Rivera Court at the Detroit Institute of Arts, showing the Detroit Industry murals in their architectural setting. The murals date to 1932–1933.

readingImages.title: Hitsville U.S.A.
readingImages.caption: The Hitsville U.S.A. buildings in Detroit, photographed in June 2006. The preserved place anchors the history of Motown and the work of keeping its story.
readingImages.credit: Blob4000 at English Wikipedia Later versions were uploaded by FuriousFreddy at en.wikipedia.

readingImages.title: Lafayette Park after redevelopment
readingImages.caption: A 2006 view of Lafayette Park redevelopment in the former Black Bottom area. This shows a later landscape, not the vanished neighborhood before clearance.

readingImages.title: Michigan Central Station — a later chapter
readingImages.caption: Michigan Central Station photographed in July 2026, after its restoration. A contemporary image for the reading about reuse and continuing change.

readingImages.title: Public space on the riverfront
readingImages.caption: Rivard Place on Detroit’s riverfront, April 2008, with its promenade and carousel. Context for public waterfront access; this is not the newer Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Centennial Park.

readingImages.title: La Placita in El Pueblo
readingImages.caption: La Placita church at El Pueblo, photographed in July 2007. A surviving landmark of the city’s layered history, not a depiction of the earlier Tongva village.

readingImages.title: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
readingImages.caption: Cover and seal of the treaty’s exchange copy, 1848. A historical document for the reading about the changing border and sovereignty.

readingImages.title: Water arriving through the aqueduct system
readingImages.caption: The Second Los Angeles Aqueduct Cascades at Sylmar, photographed in September 2008. This later part of the system illustrates water infrastructure; it is not the 1913 opening of the original aqueduct.

readingImages.title: Union Station and its rail approaches
readingImages.caption: A modern overhead view of Los Angeles Union Station. The photograph shows the surviving station, not the earlier Chinatown displaced by development.

readingImages.title: Berry Gordy — a creative connection
readingImages.caption: Motown founder Berry Gordy at a performance of The Hot Chocolate Nutcracker in December 2010. A later portrait connected to the organization’s history, not a photograph of its 1972 move to Los Angeles.

readingImages.title: Japanese American National Museum
readingImages.caption: The museum in Little Tokyo, photographed in November 2010. A place of remembrance; this is not an image of forced removal in 1942 or a claim that the cited 2022 exhibition is still running.

readingImages.title: The Great Wall of Los Angeles
readingImages.caption: The northern end of the Great Wall, photographed in December 2024. A view of the mural’s setting and its more recent timeline sections.

readingImages.title: Lupines on former railway land
readingImages.caption: Lupines at Rio de Los Angeles State Park, March 2010. The park occupies part of the former Taylor Yard landscape; this is contextual imagery, not a photograph or rendering of the proposed Paseo del Rio project.

readingImages.title: A female athlete stands confidently in a gritty gym with worn walls, wearing a black sports top and shorts. She appears ready for a workout, showcasing her fitness dedication.
readingImages.caption: Existing gym photograph retained as general exercise context. It does not document a particular study or establish the effectiveness of a program.

readingImages.title: Kettlebell squat — strength-training context
readingImages.caption: A person performing a kettlebell squat. Relevant exercise context for the discussion of physical training; the photograph is not evidence that one training strategy outperforms another.
